title: Grid R-CNN
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings

problem.summary: Detectors localize boxes by regressing offsets through fully connected layers, which collapses the spatial layout of the feature map into a vector and loses explicit spatial information, so localization quality is poor under strict IoU criteria. Point-based localization is also fragile because the corner points of an object often lie outside the object body, where the local features are just background.
statements: The typical localization module is an FC-layer regression branch that predicts offsets of a proposal or anchor from high-level feature maps, discarding explicit spatial layout.
Locations of corner points do not directly correspond to local features: an object's corner can lie outside the object on background with features similar to nearby pixels.
Regressed boxes lack guidance from explicit spatial information, limiting accuracy at high IoU thresholds.

evidence.quote: Typical bounding box localization module is a regression branch, which is designed as several fully connected layers and takes in high-level feature maps to predict the offset of the candidate box (proposal or predefined anchor).
However the prediction is not easy because the location of the points are not directly corresponding to the local features.
the upper right corner point of the cat in Figure 1.b lies outside of the object body and its neighborhood region in the image only contains background
Grid R-CNN can determine more accurate object bounding box than regression method which lacks the guidance of explicit spatial information.

background.summary: Grid R-CNN is positioned inside the two-stage R-CNN lineage (SPP-Net, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN, R-FCN, FPN, Mask R-CNN) and contrasts itself with the one-stage keypoint detector CornerNet: it keeps the top-down two-stage pipeline but replaces only the regression branch with a grid-point branch, using no extra annotation.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: base framework whose regression branch is replaced
relatedWork.quote: Later, FasterRCNN [3] was proposed to solve this problem by utilizing a light region proposal network(RPN) to generate a sparse set of RoIs.

relatedWork.name: FPN
relatedWork.relation: feature pyramid architecture used on top of backbones
relatedWork.quote: FPN [4] proposed a top-down architecture with lateral connections for building high-level semantic feature maps for variant scales.

relatedWork.name: Mask R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: closest two-stage extension; differs by adding a mask branch instead of a grid branch
relatedWork.quote: Mask R-CNN [5] extended Faster R-CNN by adding a branch for predicting an pixel-wise object mask in parallel with the original bounding box recognition branch.

relatedWork.name: CornerNet
relatedWork.relation: prior keypoint-based detector, but one-stage bottom-up without instance definition
relatedWork.quote: CornerNet [9] is a single-stage object detector which uses paired key-points to locate the bounding box of the objects.

relatedWork.name: R-FCN
relatedWork.relation: prior fully convolutional region-based detector and VOC baseline
relatedWork.quote: R-FCN [12] proposed to use region-based fully convolution network to replace the original fully connected network.

relatedWork.name: SPP-Net and Fast R-CNN
relatedWork.quote: Then SPP-Net [11] and Fast-RCNN [2] introduced a new way to save redundant computation by extracting every region feature from the shared feature generated by entire image.

evidence.quote: Different from Mask R-CNN which extends Faster R-CNN by adding a mask branch, our method replaces the regression branch with a new grid branch to locate objects more accurately. Also, our methods need no extra annotation other than bounding box.
Since our new approach is based on two stage object detector, here we briefly review some related works.

solution.summary: Grid R-CNN replaces the offset regression branch with a fully convolutional grid branch: RoIAlign features are refined by dilated convolutions and deconvolutions into 56x56 N-by-N probability heatmaps supervised at grid-point locations, box edges are then computed as probability-weighted averages of the predicted grid points. Two-order feature fusion exchanges information between neighboring grid points' feature maps, and an extended region mapping makes the heatmap cover a twice-larger image region so out-of-proposal grid points are still labeled.
solution.approach: Predict N-by-N heatmap locations of grid points for each RoI with an FCN branch, fuse neighbor grid-point features in two orders, and take probability-weighted averages of grid points on each box edge as the box coordinates.
components: grid prediction branch: RoIAlign 14x14, eight 3x3 dilated convs, two 2x deconvolutions, N-by-N heatmaps at 56x56
multi-point supervision with 5 positive pixels in a cross shape and binary cross-entropy loss
probability-weighted aggregation of grid points per box edge
first-order and second-order grid points feature fusion with per-point filter groups
extended region mapping covering a twice larger region than the proposal
inference pipeline: RPN RoIs, NMS at 0.5 IoU, top-125 RoIs into the grid branch, final NMS

evidence.quote: the traditional regression formulation is replaced by a grid point guided localization mechanism.
Grid R-CNN divides the object bounding box region into grids and employs a fully convolutional network (FCN) [7] to predict the locations of grid points.
we design a multi-point supervision formulation to encode more clues in order to reduce the impact of inaccurate prediction of specific points.
we propose a two-stage information fusion strategy to fuse feature maps of neighbor grid points.
The grid prediction branch outputs N × N heatmaps with 56 × 56 resolution, and a pixel-wise sigmoid function is applied on each heatmap to obtain the probability map.
we re-define the representation area of the output heatmap as a twice larger corresponding region in the image

experiments.summary: Ablations on COCO minival study grid size (2/4/9 points), fusion order and extended region mapping; the method is then compared with Faster R-CNN and FPN on PASCAL VOC (COCO-style criterion) and COCO minival across ResNet-50/101, and evaluated on COCO test-dev against state-of-the-art one- and two-stage detectors with ResNet-101 and ResNeXt-101 FPN backbones.

minival, Grid R-CNN w FPN, ResNet-101 (FPN baseline 39.5)
minival, Grid R-CNN w FPN, ResNet-50 (FPN baseline 40.3)
test-dev, Grid R-CNN w FPN, ResNet-101
test-dev, Grid R-CNN w FPN, ResNeXt-101

evidence.quote: it achieves a 4.1% AP gain at IoU=0.8 and a 10.0% AP gain at IoU=0.9 on COCO benchmark compared to Faster R-CNN with Res50 backbone and FPN architecture.
our Grid R-CNN significantly improve AP over FPN and R-FCN by 3.6% and 9.7% respectively.
Compared with Faster R-CNN framework, Grid R-CNN improves AP over baseline by 2.1% with ResNet-50 backbone.
Grid R-CNN outperforms regression at higher IoU thresholds (greater than 0.7).

limitations.summary: Improvements concentrate at strict IoU thresholds while AP50 slightly drops, round-shaped object categories can even regress because grid points are rectangular, the extra grid branch adds an inference stage with its own NMS, and scale selection/cascade machinery from other detectors is not yet integrated.
items: AP50 is slightly lower than the regression baseline (e.g. 59.3 to 58.3 on FPN ResNet-50), suggesting the grid branch can slightly hurt the classification branch.
Categories with round shapes without structural edges (sports ball, frisbee, bowl, clock, cup) show declines or the least gains.
Techniques such as SNIP-style scale selection and Cascade R-CNN cascading are not applied in the current framework.
Simply enlarging proposals to cover grid points brings no gain and harms small-object accuracy, requiring the extended region mapping workaround.

evidence.quote: the results of AP0.5 indicates that grid branch may slightly affect the performance of the classification branch.
the categories suffering declines or having least gains usually have a round shape without structural edges (e.g. sports ball, frisbee, bowl, clock and cup).
since the techniques such as scaling used in SNIP [28] and cascading in Cascade R-CNN [6] are not applied in current framework of Grid R-CNN, there is still room for large improvement
Experiments show that simply enlarging the proposal area brings no gain but harms the accuracy of small objects detection.

futureDirections.direction: Combine scale selection (SNIP-style) and cascade techniques with Grid R-CNN for further gains.
futureDirections.quote: we will try to combine the scale selection and cascade techniques with Grid R-CNN and we believe a further gain can be obtained.

futureDirections.direction: Design circle-shaped point layouts to better localize round objects.
futureDirections.quote: we are inspired to design points in circle shapes for better localization of objects with a round shape in future works.

equations.name: Heatmap-to-image point mapping
equations.expr: linear rescaling of heatmap coordinates (Hx, Hy) to input-image coordinates (Ix, Iy) using the proposal position and size

equations.name: Box edge from grid points
equations.expr: xl = (1/N) * sum_{j in E1} xj*pj (probability-weighted average over grid points on the edge; similarly xr, yu, yb)

equations.name: First-order feature fusion
equations.expr: Fi' = Fi + sum_{j in Si} T_{j->i}(Fj)

equations.name: Extended region mapping
equations.expr: same linear mapping as Eq 1 but with the heatmap representation area re-defined as a twice larger image region
